explanation: Brazil is a tactile, affectionate culture — hugging, cheek-kissing, hand-holding, and standing close while talking are all normal in social settings, reflecting a much smaller personal-space bubble than in the US or Northern Europe. Brazilians also generally hold relaxed attitudes toward the body (seen in beachwear and Carnival costumes), so moderate PDA attracts little attention; very formal or professional settings call for more restraint.
local_tip: Don't be surprised by close physical contact when greeting — reciprocate warmly with a cheek kiss or hug rather than stepping back, which can come across as cold.
regional_note: Cheek-kiss greetings vary by region: one kiss is typical in São Paulo, two in Rio de Janeiro, and three or more in Bahia and other parts of the Northeast.

also_check.note: Public affection is highly restrained; even hand-holding can feel out of place in formal settings.
Public affection between unmarried couples is culturally taboo and can carry legal risk.
Cheek-kissing (la bise) is a standard greeting, and moderate PDA is widely accepted socially.
